name: Data Store Layer
description: Describes physical persistence: databases and schemas, tables and collections, columns and fields, indexes, constraints, views, migrations, access patterns and the queries that read and write them (ISO/IEC 9075 SQL with extensions for document, key-value and graph paradigms). Migration scripts, table definitions and repository or DAO code that talks to storage are evidence for elements here. Modelling rules: containment is one level at a time: a database composes namespaces, or collections and views directly when the engine has none; a namespace composes collections, views, stored logic and nested namespaces; a collection composes its fields, indexes, validation rules and event handlers, and may compose partitions. Stored data is passive: collections, views, fields and databases are accessed, referenced and mapped, and never serve or trigger; application components, functions and services access the collections and views they read and write. Behaviour inside the store is stored logic, event handlers and access patterns: event handlers are attached to a collection, reference the fields they watch and trigger stored logic; stored logic accesses collections, triggers other stored logic and refreshes views; access patterns access a collection, use indexes and reference the fields in their key and filter conditions, and serve the application functions that issue them. Validation rules reference the fields they constrain, and a foreign key cascades to the collection it references. Views derive from collections and views; retention policies govern collections and namespaces, archive to collections and trigger the stored logic that purges them. Across layers, the store reaches the business through the application layer and the data model: stored logic realizes application functions, event handlers trigger application events, object schemas map to collections, and a collection may realize a business object as a shortcut; a view maps to the API response it backs.
